region.name: Cameroon and the Lake Chad basin
region.why: Forest, savanna and Sahel in one country: where is the land gaining or losing its growing season?

lgp.label: Growing season
lgp.simple: How many days a year crops can grow on rain alone: days when the rain brings at least half of the water the air could evaporate, plus the days the soil keeps feeding the plants after the rains, with the air above 5 °C.
lgp.method: FAO length of growing period (FAO 1978, GAEZ): monthly rain, potential evaporation and temperature interpolated to days; a day grows when rain >= 0.5 x potential evaporation or a 100 mm soil store still holds water
lgp.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

aridity.label: Aridity index
aridity.simple: Rain divided by the water the air could evaporate. Below 0.65 the land is a dryland, below 0.5 semi-arid, below 0.2 arid (UNEP).
aridity.method: P / PET (UNEP 1992); PET by Hargreaves & Samani (1985), FAO-56 eq. 52, from the averages of the daily maximum and minimum temperature and the sunlight at the top of the atmosphere
aridity.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

soil_root.label: Root-zone soil wetness
soil_root.simple: How wet the soil is where roots drink (about the top metre): 0 % bone dry, 100 % soaked.
soil_root.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

soil_top.label: Surface soil wetness
soil_top.simple: How wet the top 5 cm of soil are, where seeds germinate.
soil_top.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

surface_temp.label: Surface temperature
surface_temp.simple: The temperature of the ground itself. In the tropics a hotter surface means more heat stress for crops and more water lost to the air.
surface_temp.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

rain.label: Rain
rain.simple: How much rain falls in a year.
rain.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

pet.label: Potential evaporation
pet.simple: How much water the air could pull out of a wet field in a year: the thirst of the air, which grows with heat.
pet.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

erosivity.label: Rain erosivity
erosivity.simple: How aggressive the rain is for bare soil: the same yearly rain is more erosive when it falls in a few heavy months.
erosivity.method: modified Fournier index (Arnoldus 1980): sum of monthly rain squared / annual rain
erosivity.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

wind_erosion.label: Wind erosion factor
wind_erosion.simple: How strongly the climate lets the wind blow dry soil away: strong wind in months when the air is much thirstier than the rain.
wind_erosion.method: FAO (1979) climatic factor C = 1/100 x sum of u^3 x (PET - P) / PET x days, u the wind at 2 m
wind_erosion.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

albedo.label: Surface albedo
albedo.simple: The share of sunlight the surface reflects: bare, dry soil is bright, dense plants are dark.
albedo.method: annual mean of ALLSKY_SRF_ALB, nearest 1° cell

evaporation.label: Evaporation from land
evaporation.simple: Water rising from soil, lakes and plant leaves into the air.
evaporation.source: MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO) via NASA POWER

npp.label: Plant productivity (MODIS)
npp.simple: How much carbon the plants fixed in a year: how much they actually grew, seen from space.
npp.method: MOD17A3HGF net primary productivity, mean of the vegetated pixels within 5 km

params.GWETROOT: root-zone soil wetness (0-1): the water plants drink
params.GWETTOP: surface soil wetness (0-1): the top 5 cm
params.T2M_MAX_AVG: average daily maximum of the air temperature (°C): potential evaporation
params.T2M_MIN_AVG: average daily minimum of the air temperature (°C): potential evaporation
params.WS2M: wind speed at 2 m (m/s): wind erosion
params.ALLSKY_SRF_ALB: surface albedo (0-1, CERES, 1° grid): how much sunlight the surface reflects
params.EVLAND: evaporation from land (mm/day): soil, lakes and plant transpiration
